headline: A fading storm brings only a few hundredths of an inch of light rain from about Everett south on Wednesday, then Thursday and Friday turn dry with morning fog, ahead of a possibly showery weekend and a likely rainy front on Tuesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Wednesday stays cloudy, with breezy east winds in the Cascade foothills and gusty east winds through the Strait of Juan de Fuca that ease during the afternoon. A weakening front pushes light rain north from Oregon, but forecasters only carry rain chances as far north as about Everett by late afternoon, so the north Olympic Peninsula and northern Sound are unlikely to see much; anywhere it does rain, totals will be just a few hundredths of an inch. Highs will be fairly uniform near 50. Light rain remains possible from Everett southward Wednesday evening as the front falls apart overnight, with lows in the low 30s to low 40s.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Thursday will be mostly dry, though a stray shower can't be fully ruled out with the weakened storm lingering over western Oregon; fog forms in the morning over the southwest interior and in river valleys, then clears by afternoon, with highs again near 50. High pressure moves overhead Thursday night into Friday, clearing the skies. Friday morning turns colder, with lows in the upper 20s and 30s and freezing fog in the southwest interior, then sunny skies and highs near 50 once the fog burns off by afternoon.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Another storm is expected to stall off the Oregon coast this weekend, sending bands of moisture toward Western Washington; most model runs keep it far enough offshore that the area gets only glancing blows, but if it parks closer, showers become much more likely. Expect a chance of showers Saturday through Monday, then rain is likely Tuesday as the storm fades Monday and an organized front arrives. Snow levels around 2,500 feet this weekend mean any precipitation in the Cascade passes falls as snow; snow levels rise to 3,000 to 4,000 feet Monday night and Tuesday, but east winds through the passes could trap cold air there even with snow levels above pass level. Highs stay in the mid 40s to low 50s with lows in the 30s, and no river flooding is expected over the next 7 days.

coast: Seas in the coastal waters build to 10 to 14 feet Wednesday morning, then drop below 10 feet Thursday. A Gale Warning covers the outer coastal waters (10 to 60 miles out) until 10 AM Wednesday, followed by a Small Craft Advisory there until 4 AM Thursday; the inner coastal waters (out 10 miles) are under a Small Craft Advisory until 4 AM Thursday, the Central Strait and West Entrance of the Strait of Juan de Fuca until 4 PM Wednesday, and the Grays Harbor Bar until 3 AM Thursday as seas there build just above 10 feet. Thursday and Friday look calm on the water. This weekend a storm clipping the waters brings a 70% or higher chance of Small Craft Advisory winds on the coast and 50 to 60% in the Strait, with seas of 10 to 13 feet; a stronger system Monday and Tuesday brings a 70% or higher chance of gales on the coast, a 50 to 65% chance in the Strait, a 25 to 35% chance of storm-force gusts in the coastal waters, and seas of 12 to 16 feet.
watch_for: Where the weekend storm stalls: farther offshore means just a few showers, closer in means a wetter weekend and snow in the Cascade passes.
Freezing fog Friday morning in the southwest interior.
Tuesday's front: likely rain, possible trapped cold air in the passes, and gale-force winds on the water.
confidence: Forecasters say the forecast through Friday is on track with no changes needed; models are in somewhat better agreement for the weekend, though rain chances still hinge on where the offshore storm stalls, and they agree well on an organized front arriving Tuesday.
